title: Flow
description: One network connection the sensor observed leaving the machine. A declared egress point says the code can reach a provider and an event says it did; a flow says bytes left, whether or not anything in the code explains them.
$comment: Metadata only. There is no field for payload bytes and none will be added: the sensor sees destinations, not contents, and the moment it could record contents it would become the leak it was deployed to find.

host_id.description: Machine the sensor ran on. Not a hostname: a stable opaque id, so a report does not carry infrastructure naming.

netns.description: Network namespace, so container traffic is not confused with host traffic.

t_start_bucket.description: Observation start, rounded to a fixed bucket. A raw microsecond stamp would put wall clock into an identity that has to compare equal across runs.

resolved_host.description: Destination name, when one could be established.

resolved_host_source.description: How the name was established. Reported because the two sources can disagree and a reader needs to know which one produced this.

sni_source.description: Required. encrypted_client_hello means the name is genuinely unavailable rather than merely missing, and the two must not read alike.

process_attribution.description: How the owning process was determined. Kernel context is certain; an inference from a socket table snapshot is not, and a flow nobody could attribute is still reported.

pid_start_time.description: Guards against pid reuse: a pid alone can name two different processes over a long observation.

flow_scope.description: Which bucket this flow falls into. Only in_scope can produce an unmatched traffic finding. The other three never enter false positive accounting and are never hidden either: a bucket that disappears from the report is a silent swallow, which is what the counting was meant to prevent.

degraded_reasons.description: pre_existing_connection means bytes_out and duration_ms are lower bounds and t_start_bucket is when observation began, not when the connection did. A threshold rule must not discard such a record for falling under a limit.
